To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

feeding calcium soaps (bypass fat at 4% level) in the diet of lactating cross bred cows improved the milk yield, milk quality and digestibility of ether extract without affecting the digestability of DM, OM and CP.
feeding calcium salts of palm fatty acid (bypass fat), at 4% level, to lactating crossbred dairy cows improved milk production and milk fat quality without affecting digestibility of nutrients.

the inclusion of calcium salts of fatty acids at 4% level improved the milk production, milk quality and nutrient utilization without affecting the nutrient digestibility in lactating cross bred cows.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of calcium salts of fatty acids on milk production and quality in crossbred dairy cows.
the effect of feeding bypass fat on milk yield and milk composition of lactating cross bred cows.
the effect of feeding bypass fat (calcium salts of palm oil) on milk production, milk composition, nutrient utilization and fatty acid profile of milk in lactating cross bred cows.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the supplementation of calcium salts of Palm oil fatty acid at a 4 percent level in concentrate mixture of lactate crossbred cows improved milk production and milk fatty acid profile without affecting the digestiblity of nutrients.
the supplementation of calcium salts of fatty acids of palm oil in the concentrate mixture improved the milk yield and milk quality without affecting the nutrient digestibility.
calcium salts of palm fatty acids (bypass fat) could improve milk yield of lactating crossbreds cows without affecting the digestiblity of nutrients.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
feeding calcium soaps at 4% level improved milk production, milk fat yield, milk protein yield, milk lactose yield, SNF yield and 4% FPCM yield.

the use of calcium soaps of Palm oil fatty acids in the concentrate mixture for lactating crossbred dairy cattle improved milk production, milk quality in terms poly unsaturated fatty acids and nutrient utilization without affecting digestibility of nutrients.
the use of calcium salts of fatty acids as a supplement to the diet of dairy cows is beneficial in terms of increasing the milk yield without affecting the nutrient digestibility.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the use of palm oil fatty-acid calcium soaps as a feed supplement in dairy cattle can be an effective strategy for improving the quality of milk and milk fat, and also for increasing milk production.
the inclusion of palm oil fatty acyl esters in the diet of lactating cows is beneficial in increasing the polyunsaturated fatty acid content of milk fat.
the calcium salts of palm fatty acids can be used to improve the milk production and quality in crossbred cows.
